reviewer.summary: The fix is minimal and sits in the right layer. It adds the existing `util.nearing_recursion_limit()` guard, already used by the blockquote processor, to `OListProcessor.test`, which `UListProcessor` inherits, and to `ListIndentProcessor.test`. Near the stack limit, list markers fall through to paragraph handling, so deep input degrades instead of raising. The full suite passes. In my own probes none of the deep inputs raised under the default, `extra` and `sane_lists` configurations. These included `'- '*5000`, mixed markers, and 1000 lines indented 4 spaces each. Shallow nested-list output matched the pre-change processors on the inputs I compared. The PR's tests cover the issue's three cases plus mixed nesting, a lowered recursion limit, converter reuse, and unchanged shallow output. I found no tests deleted or loosened. The only finding is minor: the blockquote test asserts little.

decision.why: every checklist item is true and there is no blocker/major finding
